title: I Let the Community Cold-Plunge Wristband Survive Three Evenings After They Waived the Desk

parts.text: I opened the cold-plunge desk at 6:04 p.m. and host Amos had already waived the wristband from the list. The board said: WRISTBANDS STAY WITH THE SLOT. GUEST PINS ARE NIGHTLY. I was thirty, spa secretary, holding a checkout that listed our numbered bands. Amos shrugged. "Hosts are the plunge." I photographed the board, the waived list, and an unrecognized phone on the guest PIN. Then I asked for the band log. At 6:12 the desk pinged a PIN from a number we did not know.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: An unrecognized phone just used the guest PIN toward the plunge stack.

social.video_title: They waived the cold-plunge desk and used a guest PIN — Part 1/3
social.description: Cold-plunge desk, a waived list, a guest PIN on an unknown phone. Would you have asked for the band log?

parts.text: Tuesday they were at the plunge cabinet with our numbered bands. I printed Monday's PIN still and taped it to the board. Amos called it atmosphere. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. The board now has the still. At 6:18 the desk asked why the guest PIN opened the plunge stack two nights running. Amos said optics. Optics is a word hosts use when a desk exists.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: They are at the plunge cabinet; the board now has the still.

social.video_title: The guest PIN opened the plunge stack two nights — Part 2/3
social.description: Plunge cabinet, numbered bands, a still on the board. Was atmosphere ever a desk?

parts.text: Thursday the board added a second line: HOSTS ARE NOT THE PLUNGE. Amos ran his own guest PIN and told the next host atmosphere was always about optics. I keep our bands on a labeled hook. The desk is back on the list. Amos brown-bags his PINs. The cabinet finally looks like a slot, not a waiver. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Hosts are not the plunge — Part 3/3
social.description: Second line on the board, desk restored, guest PINs nightly. Was the plunge stack ever atmosphere?
